[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)impl<T: JsGeneric> Array<T> {
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)    /// Collect an iterator into a typed `Array<T>`, projecting each item
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)    /// through its canonical [`JsGeneric`] via [`IntoJsGeneric`].
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)    ///
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)    /// This is the typed counterpart to the stable
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)    /// `impl FromIterator<A> for Array where A: AsRef<JsValue>`, which always
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)    /// produces an erased `Array<JsValue>`. Use `from_iter_typed` when you
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)    /// want the element type inferred from the iterator item:
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)    ///
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)    /// ```ignore
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)    /// use js_sys::{Array, Number};
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)    ///
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)    /// let arr = Array::from_iter_typed((0..10).map(Number::from));
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)    /// // arr: Array<Number>
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)    /// ```
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)    ///
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)    /// Reference iteration (`Item = &U`) is supported transparently via the
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)    /// `&U: IntoJsGeneric` blanket in `wasm-bindgen` core.
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)    //
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)    // TODO(next major): replace the stable `FromIterator` impl above with
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)    // this behaviour and remove `from_iter_typed`.
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)    pub fn from_iter_typed<A, I>(iter: I) -> Array<T>
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)    where
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)        A: IntoJsGeneric<JsCanon = T>,
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)        I: IntoIterator<Item = A>,
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)    {
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)        let mut out = Array::<T>::new_typed();
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)        out.extend_typed(iter);
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)        out
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)    }
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)    /// Extend a typed `Array<T>` with an iterator of items convertible to
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)    /// `T` via [`IntoJsGeneric`]. Companion to [`Array::from_iter_typed`].
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)    //
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)    // TODO(next major): replace the stable `Extend` impl above with this
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    // behaviour and remove `extend_typed`.
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)    pub fn extend_typed<A, I>(&mut self, iter: I)

[2523](https://docs.rs#2523)/// The `Atomics` object provides atomic operations as static methods.
[2524](https://docs.rs#2524)/// They are used with `SharedArrayBuffer` objects.
[2525](https://docs.rs#2525)///
[2526](https://docs.rs#2526)/// The Atomic operations are installed on an `Atomics` module. Unlike
[2527](https://docs.rs#2527)/// the other global objects, `Atomics` is not a constructor. You cannot
[2528](https://docs.rs#2528)/// use it with a new operator or invoke the `Atomics` object as a
[2529](https://docs.rs#2529)/// function. All properties and methods of `Atomics` are static
[2530](https://docs.rs#2530)/// (as is the case with the Math object, for example).
[2531](https://docs.rs#2531)/// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Atomics)
[2532](https://docs.rs#2532)#[allow(non_snake_case)]

[2539](https://docs.rs#2539)        /// position in the array and returns the old value at that position.

[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)        /// until the modified value is written back.

[2764](https://docs.rs#2764)        /// that the caller is spinning while waiting on access to a shared resource. This allows the system
[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)        /// to reduce the resources allocated to the core (such as power) or thread, without yielding the
[2766](https://docs.rs#2766)        /// current thread.
[2767](https://docs.rs#2767)        ///
[2768](https://docs.rs#2768)        /// `pause()` has no observable behavior other than timing. The exact behavior is dependent on the CPU
[2769](https://docs.rs#2769)        /// architecture and the operating system. For example, in Intel x86, it may be a pause instruction as
[2770](https://docs.rs#2770)        /// per Intel's optimization manual. It could be a no-op in certain platforms.
[2771](https://docs.rs#2771)        ///
[2772](https://docs.rs#2772)        /// This method is used to operate on a `BigInt64Array` or a `BigUint64Array`.
[2773](https://docs.rs#2773)        ///

[3759](https://docs.rs#3759)    #[wasm_bindgen(extends = Object, is_type_of = JsValue::is_function, no_upcast, typescript_type = "Function")]
[3760](https://docs.rs#3760)    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[3761](https://docs.rs#3761)    /// `Function` represents any generic Function in JS, by treating all arguments as `JsValue`.
[3762](https://docs.rs#3762)    ///
[3763](https://docs.rs#3763)    /// It takes a generic parameter of phantom type `fn (Arg1, ..., Argn) -> Ret` which
[3764](https://docs.rs#3764)    /// is used to type the JS function. For example, `Function<fn () -> Number>` represents
[3765](https://docs.rs#3765)    /// a function taking no arguments that returns a number.
[3766](https://docs.rs#3766)    ///
[3767](https://docs.rs#3767)    /// The 8 generic argument parameters (`Arg1` through `Arg8`) are the argument
[3768](https://docs.rs#3768)    /// types. Arguments not provided enable strict arity checking at compile time.
[3769](https://docs.rs#3769)    ///
[3770](https://docs.rs#3770)    /// A void function is represented by `fn (Arg) -> Undefined`, and **not** the `()` unit
[3771](https://docs.rs#3771)    /// type. This is because generics must be based on JS values in the JS generic type system.
[3772](https://docs.rs#3772)    ///
[3773](https://docs.rs#3773)    /// _The default without any parameters is as a void function - no arguments, `Undefined` return._
[3774](https://docs.rs#3774)    ///
[3775](https://docs.rs#3775)    /// _The default generic for `Function` is `fn (JsValue, JsValue, ...) -> JsValue`,
[3776](https://docs.rs#3776)    /// representing any function, since all functions safely upcast into this function._
[3777](https://docs.rs#3777)    ///
[3778](https://docs.rs#3778)    /// ### Arity Enforcement
[3779](https://docs.rs#3779)    ///
[3780](https://docs.rs#3780)    /// It is not possible to use `call4` or `bind4` on a function that does not have
[3781](https://docs.rs#3781)    /// at least 4 arguments — the compiler will reject this because only arguments that
[3782](https://docs.rs#3782)    /// are not `None` support the trait bound for `ErasableGeneric`.
[3783](https://docs.rs#3783)    ///
[3784](https://docs.rs#3784)    /// ### Examples
[3785](https://docs.rs#3785)    ///
[3786](https://docs.rs#3786)    /// ```ignore
[3787](https://docs.rs#3787)    /// // A function taking no args, returning Number
[3788](https://docs.rs#3788)    /// let f: Function<Number> = get_some_fn();
[3789](https://docs.rs#3789)    ///
[3790](https://docs.rs#3790)    /// // A function taking (String, Number) and returning Boolean
[3791](https://docs.rs#3791)    /// let f: Function<Boolean, String, Number> = get_some_fn();
[3792](https://docs.rs#3792)    ///
[3793](https://docs.rs#3793)    /// ### Upcasting
[3794](https://docs.rs#3794)    ///
[3795](https://docs.rs#3795)    /// To pass a typed `Function` where a different generic Function is expected, `upcast()` may be used
[3796](https://docs.rs#3796)    /// to convert into any generic `Function` at zero cost with type-safety.
[3797](https://docs.rs#3797)    ///
[3798](https://docs.rs#3798)    /// MDN documentation (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function)
[3799](https://docs.rs#3799)    pub type Function<
[3800](https://docs.rs#3800)        T: JsFunction = fn(
[3801](https://docs.rs#3801)            JsValue,
[3802](https://docs.rs#3802)            JsValue,
[3803](https://docs.rs#3803)            JsValue,
[3804](https://docs.rs#3804)            JsValue,
[3805](https://docs.rs#3805)            JsValue,
[3806](https://docs.rs#3806)            JsValue,
[3807](https://docs.rs#3807)            JsValue,
[3808](https://docs.rs#3808)            JsValue,
[3809](https://docs.rs#3809)        ) -> JsValue,
[3810](https://docs.rs#3810)    >;
[3811](https://docs.rs#3811)}
[3812](https://docs.rs#3812)
[3813](https://docs.rs#3813)#[wasm_bindgen]

[3820](https://docs.rs#3820)    /// habits and allowing for more efficient code minification.
[3821](https://docs.rs#3821)    ///

[4777](https://docs.rs#4777)impl<T: JsFunction> Function<T> {
[4778](https://docs.rs#4778)    /// The `call()` method calls a function with a given `this` value and
[4779](https://docs.rs#4779)    /// arguments provided as a tuple.
[4780](https://docs.rs#4780)    ///
[4781](https://docs.rs#4781)    /// This method accepts a tuple of references matching the function's
[4782](https://docs.rs#4782)    /// argument types.
[4783](https://docs.rs#4783)    ///
[4784](https://docs.rs#4784)    /// # Example
[4785](https://docs.rs#4785)    ///
[4786](https://docs.rs#4786)    /// ```ignore
[4787](https://docs.rs#4787)    /// // 0-arg function
[4788](https://docs.rs#4788)    /// let f: Function<fn() -> Number> = get_fn();
[4789](https://docs.rs#4789)    /// let result = f.call(&JsValue::NULL, ())?;
[4790](https://docs.rs#4790)    ///
[4791](https://docs.rs#4791)    /// // 1-arg function (note trailing comma for 1-tuple)
[4792](https://docs.rs#4792)    /// let f: Function<fn(JsString) -> Number> = get_fn();
[4793](https://docs.rs#4793)    /// let result = f.call(&JsValue::NULL, (&name,))?;
[4794](https://docs.rs#4794)    ///
[4795](https://docs.rs#4795)    /// // 2-arg function
[4796](https://docs.rs#4796)    /// let f: Function<fn(JsString, Boolean) -> Number> = get_fn();
[4797](https://docs.rs#4797)    /// let result = f.call(&JsValue::NULL, (&name, &flag))?;
[4798](https://docs.rs#4798)    /// ```
[4799](https://docs.rs#4799)    ///
[4800](https://docs.rs#4800)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/call)
[4801](https://docs.rs#4801)    #[inline]
[4802](https://docs.rs#4802)    pub fn call<Args: JsArgs<T>>(&self, context: &JsValue, args: Args) -> Result<T::Ret, JsValue> {
[4803](https://docs.rs#4803)        args.apply_call(self, context)
[4804](https://docs.rs#4804)    }
[4805](https://docs.rs#4805)
[4806](https://docs.rs#4806)    /// The `bind()` method creates a new function that, when called, has its
[4807](https://docs.rs#4807)    /// `this` keyword set to the provided value, with a given sequence of
[4808](https://docs.rs#4808)    /// arguments preceding any provided when the new function is called.
[4809](https://docs.rs#4809)    ///
[4810](https://docs.rs#4810)    /// This method accepts a tuple of references to bind.
[4811](https://docs.rs#4811)    ///
[4812](https://docs.rs#4812)    /// # Example
[4813](https://docs.rs#4813)    ///
[4814](https://docs.rs#4814)    /// ```ignore
[4815](https://docs.rs#4815)    /// let f: Function<fn(JsString, Boolean) -> Number> = get_fn();
[4816](https://docs.rs#4816)    ///
[4817](https://docs.rs#4817)    /// // Bind no args - same signature
[4818](https://docs.rs#4818)    /// let bound: Function<fn(JsString, Boolean) -> Number> = f.bind(&ctx, ());
[4819](https://docs.rs#4819)    ///
[4820](https://docs.rs#4820)    /// // Bind one arg (use 1-tuple of references)
[4821](https://docs.rs#4821)    /// let bound: Function<fn(Boolean) -> Number> = f.bind(&ctx, (&my_string,));
[4822](https://docs.rs#4822)    ///
[4823](https://docs.rs#4823)    /// // Bind two args - becomes 0-arg function
[4824](https://docs.rs#4824)    /// let bound: Function<fn() -> Number> = f.bind(&ctx, (&my_string, &my_bool));
[4825](https://docs.rs#4825)    /// ```
[4826](https://docs.rs#4826)    ///
[4827](https://docs.rs#4827)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind)
[4828](https://docs.rs#4828)    #[inline]
[4829](https://docs.rs#4829)    pub fn bindn<Args: JsArgs<T>>(&self, context: &JsValue, args: Args) -> Args::BindOutput {
[4830](https://docs.rs#4830)        args.apply_bind(self, context)
[4831](https://docs.rs#4831)    }

[4951](https://docs.rs#4951)extern "C" {
[4952](https://docs.rs#4952)    /// The `FinalizationRegistry` object lets you request a callback when an
[4953](https://docs.rs#4953)    /// object is garbage-collected.
[4954](https://docs.rs#4954)    ///
[4955](https://docs.rs#4955)    /// `FinalizationRegistry` provides a way to request that a cleanup
[4956](https://docs.rs#4956)    /// callback get called at some point when an object registered with the
[4957](https://docs.rs#4957)    /// registry has been reclaimed (garbage-collected). Cleanup callbacks
[4958](https://docs.rs#4958)    /// are sometimes called *finalizers*.
[4959](https://docs.rs#4959)    ///
[4960](https://docs.rs#4960)    /// Avoid where possible: cleanup callbacks should not be relied upon for
[4961](https://docs.rs#4961)    /// anything essential. They are best used to reduce memory usage over the
[4962](https://docs.rs#4962)    /// course of a program for objects that benefit from cleanup. Whether,
[4963](https://docs.rs#4963)    /// when, and in what order callbacks fire is implementation-defined.
[4964](https://docs.rs#4964)    ///
[4965](https://docs.rs#4965)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/FinalizationRegistry)
[4966](https://docs.rs#4966)    #[wasm_bindgen(extends = Object, typescript_type = "FinalizationRegistry<any>")]
[4967](https://docs.rs#4967)    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[4968](https://docs.rs#4968)    pub type FinalizationRegistry;
[4969](https://docs.rs#4969)
[4970](https://docs.rs#4970)    /// Creates a new `FinalizationRegistry` with the given cleanup callback.
[4971](https://docs.rs#4971)    ///
[4972](https://docs.rs#4972)    /// The cleanup callback is invoked, at some point after a registered
[4973](https://docs.rs#4973)    /// target is garbage-collected, with the `held_value` that was passed to
[4974](https://docs.rs#4974)    /// [`FinalizationRegistry::register`]. Because callbacks may be deferred
[4975](https://docs.rs#4975)    /// or skipped entirely, the callback should normally outlive the
[4976](https://docs.rs#4976)    /// `FinalizationRegistry` (for example by being created via
[4977](https://docs.rs#4977)    /// [`Function::from_closure`]).
[4978](https://docs.rs#4978)    ///
[4979](https://docs.rs#4979)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/FinalizationRegistry/FinalizationRegistry)
[4980](https://docs.rs#4980)    #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
[4981](https://docs.rs#4981)    pub fn new(cleanup_callback: &Function<fn(JsValue) -> Undefined>) -> FinalizationRegistry;
[4982](https://docs.rs#4982)
[4983](https://docs.rs#4983)    /// Registers `target` with this `FinalizationRegistry`. When `target` is
[4984](https://docs.rs#4984)    /// reclaimed by the garbage collector the cleanup callback may be called
[4985](https://docs.rs#4985)    /// with `held_value`.
[4986](https://docs.rs#4986)    ///
[4987](https://docs.rs#4987)    /// `target` must be an object (or a non-registered symbol).
[4988](https://docs.rs#4988)    ///
[4989](https://docs.rs#4989)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/FinalizationRegistry/register)
[4990](https://docs.rs#4990)    #[wasm_bindgen(method)]
[4991](https://docs.rs#4991)    pub fn register(this: &FinalizationRegistry, target: &JsValue, held_value: &JsValue);
[4992](https://docs.rs#4992)
[4993](https://docs.rs#4993)    /// Registers `target` with this `FinalizationRegistry`, with an
[4994](https://docs.rs#4994)    /// `unregister_token` that can later be passed to
[4995](https://docs.rs#4995)    /// [`FinalizationRegistry::unregister`] to remove the registration.
[4996](https://docs.rs#4996)    ///
[4997](https://docs.rs#4997)    /// `target` and `unregister_token` must be objects (or non-registered

[5371](https://docs.rs#5371)    fn looks_like_iterator(it: &JsValue) -> bool {
[5372](https://docs.rs#5372)        #[wasm_bindgen]
[5373](https://docs.rs#5373)        extern "C" {
[5374](https://docs.rs#5374)            #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[5375](https://docs.rs#5375)            type MaybeIterator;
[5376](https://docs.rs#5376)
[5377](https://docs.rs#5377)            #[wasm_bindgen(method, getter)]
[5378](https://docs.rs#5378)            fn next(this: &MaybeIterator) -> JsValue;
[5379](https://docs.rs#5379)        }
[5380](https://docs.rs#5380)
[5381](https://docs.rs#5381)        if !it.is_object() {
[5382](https://docs.rs#5382)            return false;
[5383](https://docs.rs#5383)        }
[5384](https://docs.rs#5384)
[5385](https://docs.rs#5385)        let it = it.unchecked_ref::<MaybeIterator>();
[5386](https://docs.rs#5386)
[5387](https://docs.rs#5387)        it.next().is_function()
[5388](https://docs.rs#5388)    }

[5399](https://docs.rs#5399)    /// Any object that conforms to the JS async iterator protocol. For example,
[5400](https://docs.rs#5400)    /// something returned by `myObject[Symbol.asyncIterator]()`.
[5401](https://docs.rs#5401)    ///
[5402](https://docs.rs#5402)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for-await...of)
[5403](https://docs.rs#5403)    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[5404](https://docs.rs#5404)    #[wasm_bindgen(is_type_of = Iterator::looks_like_iterator, typescript_type = "AsyncIterator<any>")]
[5405](https://docs.rs#5405)    pub type AsyncIterator<T = JsValue>;
[5406](https://docs.rs#5406)
[5407](https://docs.rs#5407)    /// The `next()` method always has to return a Promise which resolves to an object
[5408](https://docs.rs#5408)    /// with appropriate properties including done and value. If a non-object value

[5503](https://docs.rs#5503)impl IterState {
[5504](https://docs.rs#5504)    fn new() -> IterState {
[5505](https://docs.rs#5505)        IterState { done: false }
[5506](https://docs.rs#5506)    }
[5507](https://docs.rs#5507)
[5508](https://docs.rs#5508)    fn next<T: FromWasmAbi + JsGeneric>(&mut self, js: &Iterator<T>) -> Option<Result<T, JsValue>> {
[5509](https://docs.rs#5509)        if self.done {
[5510](https://docs.rs#5510)            return None;
[5511](https://docs.rs#5511)        }
[5512](https://docs.rs#5512)        let next = match js.next() {
[5513](https://docs.rs#5513)            Ok(val) => val,
[5514](https://docs.rs#5514)            Err(e) => {
[5515](https://docs.rs#5515)                self.done = true;
[5516](https://docs.rs#5516)                return Some(Err(e));
[5517](https://docs.rs#5517)            }
[5518](https://docs.rs#5518)        };
[5519](https://docs.rs#5519)        if next.done() {
[5520](https://docs.rs#5520)            self.done = true;
[5521](https://docs.rs#5521)            None
[5522](https://docs.rs#5522)        } else {
[5523](https://docs.rs#5523)            Some(Ok(next.value()))
[5524](https://docs.rs#5524)        }
[5525](https://docs.rs#5525)    }

[5528](https://docs.rs#5528)/// Create an iterator over `val` using the JS iteration protocol and
[5529](https://docs.rs#5529)/// `Symbol.iterator`.
[5530](https://docs.rs#5530)// #[cfg(not(js_sys_unstable_apis))]
[5531](https://docs.rs#5531)pub fn try_iter(val: &JsValue) -> Result<Option<IntoIter<JsValue>>, JsValue> {
[5532](https://docs.rs#5532)    let iter_sym = Symbol::iterator();
[5533](https://docs.rs#5533)
[5534](https://docs.rs#5534)    let iter_fn = Reflect::get_symbol::<Object>(val.unchecked_ref(), iter_sym.as_ref())?;
[5535](https://docs.rs#5535)    let iter_fn: Function = match iter_fn.dyn_into() {
[5536](https://docs.rs#5536)        Ok(iter_fn) => iter_fn,
[5537](https://docs.rs#5537)        Err(_) => return Ok(None),
[5538](https://docs.rs#5538)    };
[5539](https://docs.rs#5539)
[5540](https://docs.rs#5540)    let it: Iterator = match iter_fn.call0(val)?.dyn_into() {
[5541](https://docs.rs#5541)        Ok(it) => it,
[5542](https://docs.rs#5542)        Err(_) => return Ok(None),
[5543](https://docs.rs#5543)    };
[5544](https://docs.rs#5544)
[5545](https://docs.rs#5545)    Ok(Some(it.into_iter()))
[5546](https://docs.rs#5546)}
[5547](https://docs.rs#5547)
[5548](https://docs.rs#5548)/// Trait for JavaScript types that implement the iterable protocol via `Symbol.iterator`.
[5549](https://docs.rs#5549)///
[5550](https://docs.rs#5550)/// Types implementing this trait can be iterated over using JavaScript's iteration
[5551](https://docs.rs#5551)/// protocol. The `Item` associated type specifies the type of values yielded.
[5552](https://docs.rs#5552)///
[5553](https://docs.rs#5553)/// ## Built-in Iterables
[5554](https://docs.rs#5554)///
[5555](https://docs.rs#5555)/// Many `js-sys` collection types implement `Iterable` out of the box:
[5556](https://docs.rs#5556)///
[5557](https://docs.rs#5557)/// ```ignore
[5558](https://docs.rs#5558)/// use js_sys::{Array, Map, Set};
[5559](https://docs.rs#5559)///
[5560](https://docs.rs#5560)/// // Array<T> yields T
[5561](https://docs.rs#5561)/// let arr: Array<Number> = get_numbers();
[5562](https://docs.rs#5562)/// for value in arr.iter() {
[5563](https://docs.rs#5563)///     let num: Number = value?;
[5564](https://docs.rs#5564)/// }
[5565](https://docs.rs#5565)///
[5566](https://docs.rs#5566)/// // Map<K, V> yields Array (key-value pairs)
[5567](https://docs.rs#5567)/// let map: Map<JsString, Number> = get_map();
[5568](https://docs.rs#5568)/// for entry in map.iter() {
[5569](https://docs.rs#5569)///     let pair: Array = entry?;
[5570](https://docs.rs#5570)/// }
[5571](https://docs.rs#5571)///
[5572](https://docs.rs#5572)/// // Set<T> yields T
[5573](https://docs.rs#5573)/// let set: Set<JsString> = get_set();
[5574](https://docs.rs#5574)/// for value in set.iter() {
[5575](https://docs.rs#5575)///     let s: JsString = value?;
[5576](https://docs.rs#5576)/// }
[5577](https://docs.rs#5577)/// ```
[5578](https://docs.rs#5578)///
[5579](https://docs.rs#5579)/// ## Typing Foreign Iterators
[5580](https://docs.rs#5580)///
[5581](https://docs.rs#5581)/// If you have a JavaScript value that implements the iterator protocol (has a `next()`
[5582](https://docs.rs#5582)/// method) but isn't a built-in type, you can use [`JsCast`] to cast it to [`Iterator<T>`]:
[5583](https://docs.rs#5583)///
[5584](https://docs.rs#5584)/// ```ignore
[5585](https://docs.rs#5585)/// use js_sys::Iterator;
[5586](https://docs.rs#5586)/// use wasm_bindgen::JsCast;
[5587](https://docs.rs#5587)///
[5588](https://docs.rs#5588)/// // For a value you know implements the iterator protocol
[5589](https://docs.rs#5589)/// fn process_iterator(js_iter: JsValue) {
[5590](https://docs.rs#5590)///     // Checked cast - returns None if not an iterator
[5591](https://docs.rs#5591)///     if let Some(iter) = js_iter.dyn_ref::<Iterator<Number>>() {
[5592](https://docs.rs#5592)///         for value in iter.into_iter() {
[5593](https://docs.rs#5593)///             let num: Number = value.unwrap();
[5594](https://docs.rs#5594)///             // ...
[5595](https://docs.rs#5595)///         }
[5596](https://docs.rs#5596)///     }
[5597](https://docs.rs#5597)/// }
[5598](https://docs.rs#5598)///
[5599](https://docs.rs#5599)/// // Or with unchecked cast when you're certain of the type
[5600](https://docs.rs#5600)/// fn process_known_iterator(js_iter: JsValue) {
[5601](https://docs.rs#5601)///     let iter: &Iterator<JsString> = js_iter.unchecked_ref();
[5602](https://docs.rs#5602)///     for value in iter.into_iter() {
[5603](https://docs.rs#5603)///         let s: JsString = value.unwrap();
[5604](https://docs.rs#5604)///         // ...
[5605](https://docs.rs#5605)///     }
[5606](https://docs.rs#5606)/// }
[5607](https://docs.rs#5607)/// ```
[5608](https://docs.rs#5608)///
[5609](https://docs.rs#5609)/// ## Using with `JsValue`
[5610](https://docs.rs#5610)///
[5611](https://docs.rs#5611)/// For dynamic or unknown iterables, use [`try_iter`] which returns an untyped iterator:
[5612](https://docs.rs#5612)///
[5613](https://docs.rs#5613)/// ```ignore
[5614](https://docs.rs#5614)/// fn iterate_unknown(val: &JsValue) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
[5615](https://docs.rs#5615)///     if let Some(iter) = js_sys::try_iter(val)? {
[5616](https://docs.rs#5616)///         for item in iter {
[5617](https://docs.rs#5617)///             let value: JsValue = item?;
[5618](https://docs.rs#5618)///             // Handle dynamically...
[5619](https://docs.rs#5619)///         }
[5620](https://docs.rs#5620)///     }
[5621](https://docs.rs#5621)///     Ok(())
[5622](https://docs.rs#5622)/// }
[5623](https://docs.rs#5623)/// ```
[5624](https://docs.rs#5624)///
[5625](https://docs.rs#5625)/// [`JsCast`]: wasm_bindgen::JsCast
[5626](https://docs.rs#5626)/// [`Iterator<T>`]: Iterator
[5627](https://docs.rs#5627)/// [`try_iter`]: crate::try_iter
[5628](https://docs.rs#5628)pub trait Iterable {
[5629](https://docs.rs#5629)    /// The type of values yielded by this iterable.
[5630](https://docs.rs#5630)    type Item;
[5631](https://docs.rs#5631)}

[7411](https://docs.rs#7411)impl Object {
[7412](https://docs.rs#7412)    /// Returns the `Object` value of this JS value if it's an instance of an
[7413](https://docs.rs#7413)    /// object.
[7414](https://docs.rs#7414)    ///
[7415](https://docs.rs#7415)    /// If this JS value is not an instance of an object then this returns
[7416](https://docs.rs#7416)    /// `None`.
[7417](https://docs.rs#7417)    pub fn try_from(val: &JsValue) -> Option<&Object> {
[7418](https://docs.rs#7418)        if val.is_object() {
[7419](https://docs.rs#7419)            Some(val.unchecked_ref())
[7420](https://docs.rs#7420)        } else {
[7421](https://docs.rs#7421)            None
[7422](https://docs.rs#7422)        }
[7423](https://docs.rs#7423)    }
[7424](https://docs.rs#7424)}

[7430](https://docs.rs#7430)    }

[9132](https://docs.rs#9132)        /// The `space` argument is a String or Number object that's used to insert white space into
[9133](https://docs.rs#9133)        /// the output JSON string for readability purposes. If this is a Number, it
[9134](https://docs.rs#9134)        /// indicates the number of space characters to use as white space; this number
[9135](https://docs.rs#9135)        /// is capped at 10 (if it is greater, the value is just 10). Values less than
[9136](https://docs.rs#9136)        /// 1 indicate that no space should be used. If this is a String, the string
[9137](https://docs.rs#9137)        /// (or the first 10 characters of the string, if it's longer than that) is
[9138](https://docs.rs#9138)        /// used as white space. If this parameter is not provided (or is null), no
[9139](https://docs.rs#9139)        /// white space is used.
[9140](https://docs.rs#9140)        ///
[9141](https://docs.rs#9141)        /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/stringify)
[9142](https://docs.rs#9142)        #[wasm_bindgen(catch, js_namespace = JSON, js_name = stringify)]
[9143](https://docs.rs#9143)        pub fn stringify_with_replacer_and_space(
[9144](https://docs.rs#9144)            obj: &JsValue,
[9145](https://docs.rs#9145)            replacer: &JsValue,
[9146](https://docs.rs#9146)            space: &JsValue,
[9147](https://docs.rs#9147)        ) -> Result<JsString, JsValue>;
[9148](https://docs.rs#9148)    }
[9149](https://docs.rs#9149)}

[9829](https://docs.rs#9829)    #[deprecated(note = "recommended to use dyn_ref instead which is now equivalent")]

[9832](https://docs.rs#9832)    }
[9833](https://docs.rs#9833)
[9834](https://docs.rs#9834)    /// Returns whether this string is a valid UTF-16 string.
[9835](https://docs.rs#9835)    ///
[9836](https://docs.rs#9836)    /// This is useful for learning whether `String::from(..)` will return a
[9837](https://docs.rs#9837)    /// lossless representation of the JS string. If this string contains
[9838](https://docs.rs#9838)    /// unpaired surrogates then `String::from` will succeed but it will be a
[9839](https://docs.rs#9839)    /// lossy representation of the JS string because unpaired surrogates will
[9840](https://docs.rs#9840)    /// become replacement characters.
[9841](https://docs.rs#9841)    ///
[9842](https://docs.rs#9842)    /// If this function returns `false` then to get a lossless representation
[9843](https://docs.rs#9843)    /// of the string you'll need to manually use the `iter` method (or the
[9844](https://docs.rs#9844)    /// `char_code_at` accessor) to view the raw character codes.
[9845](https://docs.rs#9845)    ///
[9846](https://docs.rs#9846)    /// For more information, see the documentation on [JS strings vs Rust
[9847](https://docs.rs#9847)    /// strings][docs]
[9848](https://docs.rs#9848)    ///
[9849](https://docs.rs#9849)    /// [docs]: https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html
[9850](https://docs.rs#9850)    pub fn is_valid_utf16(&self) -> bool {
[9851](https://docs.rs#9851)        core::char::decode_utf16(self.iter()).all(|i| i.is_ok())
[9852](https://docs.rs#9852)    }
[9853](https://docs.rs#9853)
[9854](https://docs.rs#9854)    /// Returns an iterator over the `u16` character codes that make up this JS
[9855](https://docs.rs#9855)    /// string.
[9856](https://docs.rs#9856)    ///
[9857](https://docs.rs#9857)    /// This method will call `char_code_at` for each code in this JS string,
[9858](https://docs.rs#9858)    /// returning an iterator of the codes in sequence.
[9859](https://docs.rs#9859)    pub fn iter(
[9860](https://docs.rs#9860)        &self,
[9861](https://docs.rs#9861)    ) -> impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = u16> + DoubleEndedIterator<Item = u16> + '_ {
[9862](https://docs.rs#9862)        (0..self.length()).map(move |i| self.char_code_at(i) as u16)
[9863](https://docs.rs#9863)    }
[9864](https://docs.rs#9864)
[9865](https://docs.rs#9865)    /// If this string consists of a single Unicode code point, then this method
[9866](https://docs.rs#9866)    /// converts it into a Rust `char` without doing any allocations.
[9867](https://docs.rs#9867)    ///
[9868](https://docs.rs#9868)    /// If this JS value is not a valid UTF-8 or consists of more than a single
[9869](https://docs.rs#9869)    /// codepoint, then this returns `None`.
[9870](https://docs.rs#9870)    ///
[9871](https://docs.rs#9871)    /// Note that a single Unicode code point might be represented as more than
[9872](https://docs.rs#9872)    /// one code unit on the JavaScript side. For example, a JavaScript string
[9873](https://docs.rs#9873)    /// `"\uD801\uDC37"` is actually a single Unicode code point U+10437 which
[9874](https://docs.rs#9874)    /// corresponds to a character '𐐷'.
[9875](https://docs.rs#9875)    pub fn as_char(&self) -> Option<char> {
[9876](https://docs.rs#9876)        let len = self.length();
[9877](https://docs.rs#9877)
[9878](https://docs.rs#9878)        if len == 0 || len > 2 {
[9879](https://docs.rs#9879)            return None;
[9880](https://docs.rs#9880)        }
[9881](https://docs.rs#9881)
[9882](https://docs.rs#9882)        #[cfg(not(js_sys_unstable_apis))]
[9883](https://docs.rs#9883)        let cp = self.code_point_at(0).as_f64().unwrap_throw() as u32;
[9884](https://docs.rs#9884)        #[cfg(js_sys_unstable_apis)]
[9885](https://docs.rs#9885)        let cp = self.code_point_at(0)?;
[9886](https://docs.rs#9886)
[9887](https://docs.rs#9887)        let c = core::char::from_u32(cp)?;
[9888](https://docs.rs#9888)
[9889](https://docs.rs#9889)        if c.len_utf16() as u32 == len {
[9890](https://docs.rs#9890)            Some(c)
[9891](https://docs.rs#9891)        } else {
[9892](https://docs.rs#9892)            None
[9893](https://docs.rs#9893)        }
[9894](https://docs.rs#9894)    }

[10305](https://docs.rs#10305)    /// Use grouping option for `Intl.NumberFormat`.
[10306](https://docs.rs#10306)    ///
[10307](https://docs.rs#10307)    /// Determines whether to use grouping separators, such as thousands
[10308](https://docs.rs#10308)    /// separators or thousand/lakh/crore separators.
[10309](https://docs.rs#10309)    ///
[10310](https://docs.rs#10310)    /// The default is `Min2` if notation is "compact", and `Auto` otherwise.
[10311](https://docs.rs#10311)    ///
[10312](https://docs.rs#10312)    /// Note: The string values `"true"` and `"false"` are accepted by JavaScript
[10313](https://docs.rs#10313)    /// but are always converted to the default value. Use `True` and `False`
[10314](https://docs.rs#10314)    /// variants for the boolean behavior.
[10315](https://docs.rs#10315)    ///
[10316](https://docs.rs#10316)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat/NumberFormat#usegrouping)
[10317](https://docs.rs#10317)    #[wasm_bindgen]
[10318](https://docs.rs#10318)    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[10319](https://docs.rs#10319)    pub enum UseGrouping {
[10320](https://docs.rs#10320)        /// Display grouping separators even if the locale prefers otherwise.
[10321](https://docs.rs#10321)        Always = "always",
[10322](https://docs.rs#10322)        /// Display grouping separators based on the locale preference,
[10323](https://docs.rs#10323)        /// which may also be dependent on the currency.
[10324](https://docs.rs#10324)        Auto = "auto",
[10325](https://docs.rs#10325)        /// Display grouping separators when there are at least 2 digits in a group.
[10326](https://docs.rs#10326)        Min2 = "min2",
[10327](https://docs.rs#10327)        /// Same as `Always`. Display grouping separators even if the locale prefers otherwise.
[10328](https://docs.rs#10328)        True = "true",
[10329](https://docs.rs#10329)        /// Display no grouping separators.
[10330](https://docs.rs#10330)        False = "false",
[10331](https://docs.rs#10331)    }

[13051](https://docs.rs#13051)    /// The `PromiseState` object represents the the status of the promise,
[13052](https://docs.rs#13052)    /// as used in `allSettled`.
[13053](https://docs.rs#13053)    ///
[13054](https://docs.rs#13054)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/allSettled)
[13055](https://docs.rs#13055)    #[must_use]
[13056](https://docs.rs#13056)    #[wasm_bindgen(extends = Object, typescript_type = "any")]
[13057](https://docs.rs#13057)    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[13058](https://docs.rs#13058)    pub type PromiseState<T = JsValue>;
[13059](https://docs.rs#13059)
[13060](https://docs.rs#13060)    /// A string, either "fulfilled" or "rejected", indicating the eventual state of the promise.
[13061](https://docs.rs#13061)    #[wasm_bindgen(method, getter = status)]
[13062](https://docs.rs#13062)    pub fn get_status<T>(this: &PromiseState<T>) -> String;
[13063](https://docs.rs#13063)
[13064](https://docs.rs#13064)    /// Only present if status is "fulfilled". The value that the promise was fulfilled with.
[13065](https://docs.rs#13065)    #[wasm_bindgen(method, getter = value)]
[13066](https://docs.rs#13066)    pub fn get_value<T>(this: &PromiseState<T>) -> Option<T>;
[13067](https://docs.rs#13067)
[13068](https://docs.rs#13068)    /// Only present if status is "rejected". The reason that the promise was rejected with.
[13069](https://docs.rs#13069)    #[wasm_bindgen(method, getter = reason)]
[13070](https://docs.rs#13070)    pub fn get_reason<T>(this: &PromiseState<T>) -> Option<JsValue>;
[13071](https://docs.rs#13071)}
[13072](https://docs.rs#13072)
[13073](https://docs.rs#13073)impl<T> PromiseState<T> {
[13074](https://docs.rs#13074)    pub fn is_fulfilled(&self) -> bool {
[13075](https://docs.rs#13075)        self.get_status() == "fulfilled"
[13076](https://docs.rs#13076)    }
[13077](https://docs.rs#13077)
[13078](https://docs.rs#13078)    pub fn is_rejected(&self) -> bool {
[13079](https://docs.rs#13079)        self.get_status() == "rejected"
[13080](https://docs.rs#13080)    }
[13081](https://docs.rs#13081)}
[13082](https://docs.rs#13082)
[13083](https://docs.rs#13083)/// Converts a `PromiseState<T>` into a `Result<T, JsValue>`, matching the
[13084](https://docs.rs#13084)/// spec invariant that exactly one of the fulfilled value or the rejection
[13085](https://docs.rs#13085)/// reason is populated per slot.
[13086](https://docs.rs#13086)impl<T: JsGeneric + FromWasmAbi> From<PromiseState<T>> for Result<T, JsValue> {
[13087](https://docs.rs#13087)    fn from(state: PromiseState<T>) -> Result<T, JsValue> {
[13088](https://docs.rs#13088)        if state.is_fulfilled() {
[13089](https://docs.rs#13089)            Ok(state.get_value().unwrap())
[13090](https://docs.rs#13090)        } else {
[13091](https://docs.rs#13091)            Err(state.get_reason().unwrap())
[13092](https://docs.rs#13092)        }
[13093](https://docs.rs#13093)    }

[13100](https://docs.rs#13100)    /// an asynchronous operation, and its resulting value.
[13101](https://docs.rs#13101)    ///
[13102](https://docs.rs#13102)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise)
[13103](https://docs.rs#13103)    #[must_use]

[13107](https://docs.rs#13107)
[13108](https://docs.rs#13108)    /// Creates a new `Promise` with the provided executor `cb`
[13109](https://docs.rs#13109)    ///
[13110](https://docs.rs#13110)    /// The `cb` is a function that is passed with the arguments `resolve` and
[13111](https://docs.rs#13111)    /// `reject`. The `cb` function is executed immediately by the `Promise`
[13112](https://docs.rs#13112)    /// implementation, passing `resolve` and `reject` functions (the executor
[13113](https://docs.rs#13113)    /// is called before the `Promise` constructor even returns the created
[13114](https://docs.rs#13114)    /// object). The `resolve` and `reject` functions, when called, resolve or
[13115](https://docs.rs#13115)    /// reject the promise, respectively. The executor normally initiates
[13116](https://docs.rs#13116)    /// some asynchronous work, and then, once that completes, either calls
[13117](https://docs.rs#13117)    /// the `resolve` function to resolve the promise or else rejects it if an
[13118](https://docs.rs#13118)    /// error occurred.
[13119](https://docs.rs#13119)    ///
[13120](https://docs.rs#13120)    /// If an error is thrown in the executor function, the promise is rejected.
[13121](https://docs.rs#13121)    /// The return value of the executor is ignored.
[13122](https://docs.rs#13122)    ///
[13123](https://docs.rs#13123)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise)
[13124](https://docs.rs#13124)    #[cfg(not(js_sys_unstable_apis))]
[13125](https://docs.rs#13125)    #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
[13126](https://docs.rs#13126)    pub fn new(cb: &mut dyn FnMut(Function, Function)) -> Promise;
[13127](https://docs.rs#13127)

[13425](https://docs.rs#13425)impl<T: JsGeneric> Promising for Promise<T> {
[13426](https://docs.rs#13426)    type Resolution = T;
[13427](https://docs.rs#13427)}
[13428](https://docs.rs#13428)
[13429](https://docs.rs#13429)/// Internal: maps a tuple of `Promise<T_i>` to the result shapes of
[13430](https://docs.rs#13430)/// [`Promise::all_tuple`] and [`Promise::all_settled_tuple`].
[13431](https://docs.rs#13431)///
[13432](https://docs.rs#13432)/// Implemented for every tuple arity 1..=8 of `Promise<T: JsGeneric>`. The
[13433](https://docs.rs#13433)/// associated `Joined` / `Settled` types pin down the [`ArrayTuple`] shape
[13434](https://docs.rs#13434)/// of the result so the one [`JsCast::unchecked_into`] needed to reinterpret
[13435](https://docs.rs#13435)/// the [`Array<JsValue>`] returned by `Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled`
[13436](https://docs.rs#13436)/// is encapsulated inside each impl — the caller sees a fully-typed
[13437](https://docs.rs#13437)/// `Promise<ArrayTuple<...>>`.
[13438](https://docs.rs#13438)///
[13439](https://docs.rs#13439)/// The soundness of the `unchecked_into`s here rests on `Promise.all` and
[13440](https://docs.rs#13440)/// `Promise.allSettled` preserving input order and arity, which they do by
[13441](https://docs.rs#13441)/// spec.
[13442](https://docs.rs#13442)///
[13443](https://docs.rs#13443)/// You normally call [`Promise::all_tuple`] / [`Promise::all_settled_tuple`]
[13444](https://docs.rs#13444)/// rather than using this trait directly.
[13445](https://docs.rs#13445)#[doc(hidden)]
[13446](https://docs.rs#13446)pub trait PromiseTuple {
[13447](https://docs.rs#13447)    /// The typed `ArrayTuple` shape the joined promise resolves to.
[13448](https://docs.rs#13448)    ///
[13449](https://docs.rs#13449)    /// For a tuple `(Promise<T1>, Promise<T2>, ...)` this is
[13450](https://docs.rs#13450)    /// `ArrayTuple<(T1, T2, ...)>`.
[13451](https://docs.rs#13451)    type Joined: JsGeneric;
[13452](https://docs.rs#13452)
[13453](https://docs.rs#13453)    /// The typed `ArrayTuple` shape the all-settled promise resolves to.
[13454](https://docs.rs#13454)    ///
[13455](https://docs.rs#13455)    /// For a tuple `(Promise<T1>, Promise<T2>, ...)` this is
[13456](https://docs.rs#13456)    /// `ArrayTuple<(PromiseState<T1>, PromiseState<T2>, ...)>`.
[13457](https://docs.rs#13457)    type Settled: JsGeneric;
[13458](https://docs.rs#13458)
[13459](https://docs.rs#13459)    /// Join via `Promise.all`, returning a typed `Promise`.
[13460](https://docs.rs#13460)    fn all(self) -> Promise<Self::Joined>;
[13461](https://docs.rs#13461)
[13462](https://docs.rs#13462)    /// Settle via `Promise.allSettled`, returning a typed `Promise`.
[13463](https://docs.rs#13463)    fn all_settled(self) -> Promise<Self::Settled>;
[13464](https://docs.rs#13464)}
[13465](https://docs.rs#13465)
[13466](https://docs.rs#13466)macro_rules! impl_promise_tuple {
[13467](https://docs.rs#13467)    ([$($T:ident)+] [$($idx:tt)+]) => {
[13468](https://docs.rs#13468)        // Rust tuple of `Promise<T_i>`. Builds the heterogeneous
[13469](https://docs.rs#13469)        // `ArrayTuple` of promises via the existing `From<(...)>` impl
[13470](https://docs.rs#13470)        // (each element upcasts through `JsGeneric`), then delegates to
[13471](https://docs.rs#13471)        // the `ArrayTuple` impl below.
[13472](https://docs.rs#13472)        impl<$($T: JsGeneric),+> PromiseTuple for ($(Promise<$T>,)+) {
[13473](https://docs.rs#13473)            type Joined = ArrayTuple<($($T,)+)>;
[13474](https://docs.rs#13474)            type Settled = ArrayTuple<($(PromiseState<$T>,)+)>;
[13475](https://docs.rs#13475)
[13476](https://docs.rs#13476)            fn all(self) -> Promise<Self::Joined> {
[13477](https://docs.rs#13477)                let tuple: ArrayTuple<($(Promise<$T>,)+)> = ($(self.$idx,)+).into();
[13478](https://docs.rs#13478)                tuple.all()
[13479](https://docs.rs#13479)            }
[13480](https://docs.rs#13480)
[13481](https://docs.rs#13481)            fn all_settled(self) -> Promise<Self::Settled> {
[13482](https://docs.rs#13482)                let tuple: ArrayTuple<($(Promise<$T>,)+)> = ($(self.$idx,)+).into();
[13483](https://docs.rs#13483)                tuple.all_settled()
[13484](https://docs.rs#13484)            }
[13485](https://docs.rs#13485)        }
[13486](https://docs.rs#13486)
[13487](https://docs.rs#13487)        // `ArrayTuple<(Promise<T_1>, ..., Promise<T_n>)>` — callers who
[13488](https://docs.rs#13488)        // already have an `ArrayTuple` (e.g. from a binding that returns
[13489](https://docs.rs#13489)        // one, or built via `.into()` earlier in a pipeline) can pass it
[13490](https://docs.rs#13490)        // directly without unpacking into a Rust tuple.
[13491](https://docs.rs#13491)        //
[13492](https://docs.rs#13492)        // Hands the `ArrayTuple` straight to `Promise.all_iterable` /
[13493](https://docs.rs#13493)        // `Promise.allSettled_iterable` and reinterprets the result
[13494](https://docs.rs#13494)        // `Array<JsValue>` as the intended typed `ArrayTuple`. Safe because
[13495](https://docs.rs#13495)        // `Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled` preserve input order and
[13496](https://docs.rs#13496)        // arity by spec.
[13497](https://docs.rs#13497)        impl<$($T: JsGeneric),+> PromiseTuple for ArrayTuple<($(Promise<$T>,)+)> {
[13498](https://docs.rs#13498)            type Joined = ArrayTuple<($($T,)+)>;
[13499](https://docs.rs#13499)            type Settled = ArrayTuple<($(PromiseState<$T>,)+)>;
[13500](https://docs.rs#13500)
[13501](https://docs.rs#13501)            fn all(self) -> Promise<Self::Joined> {
[13502](https://docs.rs#13502)                use wasm_bindgen::JsCast;
[13503](https://docs.rs#13503)                Promise::all_iterable(&self).unchecked_into()
[13504](https://docs.rs#13504)            }
[13505](https://docs.rs#13505)
[13506](https://docs.rs#13506)            fn all_settled(self) -> Promise<Self::Settled> {
[13507](https://docs.rs#13507)                use wasm_bindgen::JsCast;
[13508](https://docs.rs#13508)                Promise::all_settled_iterable(&self).unchecked_into()
[13509](https://docs.rs#13509)            }
[13510](https://docs.rs#13510)        }

[13523](https://docs.rs#13523)impl Promise {
[13524](https://docs.rs#13524)    /// Heterogeneous counterpart to [`Promise::all_iterable`]: accepts a Rust
[13525](https://docs.rs#13525)    /// tuple of `Promise<T_i>` and returns a single [`Promise`] resolving to a
[13526](https://docs.rs#13526)    /// typed [`ArrayTuple<(T_1, T_2, ..., T_n)>`].
[13527](https://docs.rs#13527)    ///
[13528](https://docs.rs#13528)    /// Destructure the awaited result via [`ArrayTuple::into_tuple`] to get
[13529](https://docs.rs#13529)    /// the individual values back as a native Rust tuple. Implemented for
[13530](https://docs.rs#13530)    /// arity 1..=8.
[13531](https://docs.rs#13531)    ///
[13532](https://docs.rs#13532)    /// Rejects with the first rejection, matching `Promise.all` semantics.
[13533](https://docs.rs#13533)    ///
[13534](https://docs.rs#13534)    /// # Example
[13535](https://docs.rs#13535)    ///
[13536](https://docs.rs#13536)    /// ```ignore
[13537](https://docs.rs#13537)    /// use js_sys::Promise;
[13538](https://docs.rs#13538)    ///
[13539](https://docs.rs#13539)    /// let (response, buffer) = Promise::all_tuple((fetch_promise, buffer_promise))
[13540](https://docs.rs#13540)    ///     .await?
[13541](https://docs.rs#13541)    ///     .into_tuple();
[13542](https://docs.rs#13542)    /// ```
[13543](https://docs.rs#13543)    #[inline]
[13544](https://docs.rs#13544)    pub fn all_tuple<T: PromiseTuple>(promises: T) -> Promise<T::Joined> {
[13545](https://docs.rs#13545)        promises.all()
[13546](https://docs.rs#13546)    }
[13547](https://docs.rs#13547)
[13548](https://docs.rs#13548)    /// Heterogeneous counterpart to [`Promise::all_settled_iterable`]: accepts
[13549](https://docs.rs#13549)    /// a Rust tuple of `Promise<T_i>` and returns a single [`Promise`]
[13550](https://docs.rs#13550)    /// resolving to a typed
[13551](https://docs.rs#13551)    /// `ArrayTuple<(PromiseState<T_1>, ..., PromiseState<T_n>)>`.
[13552](https://docs.rs#13552)    ///
[13553](https://docs.rs#13553)    /// Unlike [`Promise::all_tuple`], this never rejects early: every input
[13554](https://docs.rs#13554)    /// settles (fulfills or rejects) and is reflected by its [`PromiseState`]
[13555](https://docs.rs#13555)    /// slot in the result tuple. Implemented for arity 1..=8.
[13556](https://docs.rs#13556)    ///
[13557](https://docs.rs#13557)    /// # Example
[13558](https://docs.rs#13558)    ///
[13559](https://docs.rs#13559)    /// ```ignore
[13560](https://docs.rs#13560)    /// use js_sys::Promise;
[13561](https://docs.rs#13561)    ///
[13562](https://docs.rs#13562)    /// let results = Promise::all_settled_tuple((fetch_promise, buffer_promise)).await?;
[13563](https://docs.rs#13563)    /// let (response_state, buffer_state) = results.into_tuple();
[13564](https://docs.rs#13564)    /// ```
[13565](https://docs.rs#13565)    #[inline]
[13566](https://docs.rs#13566)    pub fn all_settled_tuple<T: PromiseTuple>(promises: T) -> Promise<T::Settled> {
[13567](https://docs.rs#13567)        promises.all_settled()
[13568](https://docs.rs#13568)    }
[13569](https://docs.rs#13569)}
[13570](https://docs.rs#13570)
[13571](https://docs.rs#13571)/// Returns a handle to the global scope object.
[13572](https://docs.rs#13572)///
[13573](https://docs.rs#13573)/// This allows access to the global properties and global names by accessing
[13574](https://docs.rs#13574)/// the `Object` returned.
[13575](https://docs.rs#13575)pub fn global() -> Object {
[13576](https://docs.rs#13576)    use wasm_bindgen::__rt::LazyCell;
[13577](https://docs.rs#13577)
[13578](https://docs.rs#13578)    #[cfg_attr(target_feature = "atomics", thread_local)]
[13579](https://docs.rs#13579)    static GLOBAL: LazyCell<Object> = LazyCell::new(get_global_object);
[13580](https://docs.rs#13580)
[13581](https://docs.rs#13581)    return GLOBAL.clone();
[13582](https://docs.rs#13582)
[13583](https://docs.rs#13583)    fn get_global_object() -> Object {
[13584](https://docs.rs#13584)        // Accessing the global object is not an easy thing to do, and what we
[13585](https://docs.rs#13585)        // basically want is `globalThis` but we can't rely on that existing
[13586](https://docs.rs#13586)        // everywhere. In the meantime we've got the fallbacks mentioned in:
[13587](https://docs.rs#13587)        //
[13588](https://docs.rs#13588)        // https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/globalThis
[13589](https://docs.rs#13589)        //
[13590](https://docs.rs#13590)        // Note that this is pretty heavy code-size wise but it at least gets
[13591](https://docs.rs#13591)        // the job largely done for now and avoids the `Function` constructor at
[13592](https://docs.rs#13592)        // the end which triggers CSP errors.
[13593](https://docs.rs#13593)        #[wasm_bindgen]
[13594](https://docs.rs#13594)        extern "C" {
[13595](https://docs.rs#13595)            #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[13596](https://docs.rs#13596)            type Global;
[13597](https://docs.rs#13597)
[13598](https://docs.rs#13598)            #[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2, js_name = globalThis)]
[13599](https://docs.rs#13599)            static GLOBAL_THIS: Option<Object>;
[13600](https://docs.rs#13600)
[13601](https://docs.rs#13601)            #[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2, js_name = self)]
[13602](https://docs.rs#13602)            static SELF: Option<Object>;
[13603](https://docs.rs#13603)
[13604](https://docs.rs#13604)            #[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2, js_name = window)]
[13605](https://docs.rs#13605)            static WINDOW: Option<Object>;
[13606](https://docs.rs#13606)
[13607](https://docs.rs#13607)            #[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2, js_name = global)]
[13608](https://docs.rs#13608)            static GLOBAL: Option<Object>;
[13609](https://docs.rs#13609)        }
[13610](https://docs.rs#13610)
[13611](https://docs.rs#13611)        // The order is important: in Firefox Extension Content Scripts `globalThis`
[13612](https://docs.rs#13612)        // is a Sandbox (not Window), so `globalThis` must be checked after `window`.
[13613](https://docs.rs#13613)        let static_object = SELF
[13614](https://docs.rs#13614)            .with(Option::clone)
[13615](https://docs.rs#13615)            .or_else(|| WINDOW.with(Option::clone))
[13616](https://docs.rs#13616)            .or_else(|| GLOBAL_THIS.with(Option::clone))
[13617](https://docs.rs#13617)            .or_else(|| GLOBAL.with(Option::clone));
[13618](https://docs.rs#13618)        if let Some(obj) = static_object {
[13619](https://docs.rs#13619)            if !obj.is_undefined() {
[13620](https://docs.rs#13620)                return obj;
[13621](https://docs.rs#13621)            }
[13622](https://docs.rs#13622)        }
[13623](https://docs.rs#13623)
[13624](https://docs.rs#13624)        // Global object not found
[13625](https://docs.rs#13625)        JsValue::undefined().unchecked_into()
[13626](https://docs.rs#13626)    }
[13627](https://docs.rs#13627)}

[13819](https://docs.rs#13819)    ///
[13820](https://docs.rs#13820)    /// let bits = array.to_u16_vec();
[13821](https://docs.rs#13821)    /// let values: Vec<f16> = bits.into_iter().map(f16::from_bits).collect();
[13822](https://docs.rs#13822)    /// ```
[13823](https://docs.rs#13823)    pub fn to_u16_vec(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
[13824](https://docs.rs#13824)        self.as_uint16_view().to_vec()
[13825](https://docs.rs#13825)    }

[13995](https://docs.rs#13995)            /// Creates a JS typed array which is a view into wasm's linear
[13996](https://docs.rs#13996)            /// memory at the slice specified.
[13997](https://docs.rs#13997)            ///
[13998](https://docs.rs#13998)            /// This function returns a new typed array which is a view into
[13999](https://docs.rs#13999)            /// wasm's memory. This view does not copy the underlying data.
[14000](https://docs.rs#14000)            ///
[14001](https://docs.rs#14001)            /// # Safety
[14002](https://docs.rs#14002)            ///
[14003](https://docs.rs#14003)            /// Views into WebAssembly memory are only valid so long as the
[14004](https://docs.rs#14004)            /// backing buffer isn't resized in JS. Once this function is called
[14005](https://docs.rs#14005)            /// any future calls to `Box::new` (or malloc of any form) may cause
[14006](https://docs.rs#14006)            /// the returned value here to be invalidated. Use with caution!
[14007](https://docs.rs#14007)            ///
[14008](https://docs.rs#14008)            /// Additionally the returned object can be safely mutated but the
[14009](https://docs.rs#14009)            /// input slice isn't guaranteed to be mutable.
[14010](https://docs.rs#14010)            ///
[14011](https://docs.rs#14011)            /// Finally, the returned object is disconnected from the input
[14012](https://docs.rs#14012)            /// slice's lifetime, so there's no guarantee that the data is read
[14013](https://docs.rs#14013)            /// at the right time.
[14014](https://docs.rs#14014)            pub unsafe fn view(rust: &[$ty]) -> $name {
[14015](https://docs.rs#14015)                wasm_bindgen::__rt::wbg_cast(rust)
[14016](https://docs.rs#14016)            }
[14017](https://docs.rs#14017)
[14018](https://docs.rs#14018)            /// Creates a JS typed array which is a view into wasm's linear
[14019](https://docs.rs#14019)            /// memory at the specified pointer with specified length.
[14020](https://docs.rs#14020)            ///
[14021](https://docs.rs#14021)            /// This function returns a new typed array which is a view into
[14022](https://docs.rs#14022)            /// wasm's memory. This view does not copy the underlying data.
[14023](https://docs.rs#14023)            ///
[14024](https://docs.rs#14024)            /// # Safety
[14025](https://docs.rs#14025)            ///
[14026](https://docs.rs#14026)            /// Views into WebAssembly memory are only valid so long as the
[14027](https://docs.rs#14027)            /// backing buffer isn't resized in JS. Once this function is called
[14028](https://docs.rs#14028)            /// any future calls to `Box::new` (or malloc of any form) may cause
[14029](https://docs.rs#14029)            /// the returned value here to be invalidated. Use with caution!
[14030](https://docs.rs#14030)            ///
[14031](https://docs.rs#14031)            /// Additionally the returned object can be safely mutated,
[14032](https://docs.rs#14032)            /// the changes are guaranteed to be reflected in the input array.
[14033](https://docs.rs#14033)            pub unsafe fn view_mut_raw(ptr: *mut $ty, length: usize) -> $name {
[14034](https://docs.rs#14034)                let slice = core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr, length);
[14035](https://docs.rs#14035)                Self::view(slice)
[14036](https://docs.rs#14036)            }
[14037](https://docs.rs#14037)
[14038](https://docs.rs#14038)            /// Copy the contents of this JS typed array into the destination
[14039](https://docs.rs#14039)            /// Rust pointer.
[14040](https://docs.rs#14040)            ///
[14041](https://docs.rs#14041)            /// This function will efficiently copy the memory from a typed
[14042](https://docs.rs#14042)            /// array into this Wasm module's own linear memory, initializing
[14043](https://docs.rs#14043)            /// the memory destination provided.
[14044](https://docs.rs#14044)            ///
[14045](https://docs.rs#14045)            /// # Safety
[14046](https://docs.rs#14046)            ///
[14047](https://docs.rs#14047)            /// This function requires `dst` to point to a buffer
[14048](https://docs.rs#14048)            /// large enough to fit this array's contents.
[14049](https://docs.rs#14049)            pub unsafe fn raw_copy_to_ptr(&self, dst: *mut $ty) {
[14050](https://docs.rs#14050)                let slice = core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(dst, self.length() as usize);
[14051](https://docs.rs#14051)                self.copy_to(slice);
[14052](https://docs.rs#14052)            }
[14053](https://docs.rs#14053)
[14054](https://docs.rs#14054)            /// Copy the contents of this JS typed array into the destination
[14055](https://docs.rs#14055)            /// Rust slice.
[14056](https://docs.rs#14056)            ///
[14057](https://docs.rs#14057)            /// This function will efficiently copy the memory from a typed
[14058](https://docs.rs#14058)            /// array into this Wasm module's own linear memory, initializing

[14066](https://docs.rs#14066)                core::assert_eq!(self.length() as usize, dst.len());

[14068](https://docs.rs#14068)            }
[14069](https://docs.rs#14069)
[14070](https://docs.rs#14070)            /// Copy the contents of this JS typed array into the destination
[14071](https://docs.rs#14071)            /// Rust slice.
[14072](https://docs.rs#14072)            ///
[14073](https://docs.rs#14073)            /// This function will efficiently copy the memory from a typed
[14074](https://docs.rs#14074)            /// array into this Wasm module's own linear memory, initializing

[14076](https://docs.rs#14076)            ///
[14077](https://docs.rs#14077)            /// # Panics
[14078](https://docs.rs#14078)            ///

[14081](https://docs.rs#14081)            pub fn copy_to_uninit<'dst>(&self, dst: &'dst mut [MaybeUninit<$ty>]) -> &'dst mut [$ty] {
[14082](https://docs.rs#14082)                core::assert_eq!(self.length() as usize, dst.len());
[14083](https://docs.rs#14083)                let dst = unsafe { &mut *(dst as *mut [MaybeUninit<$ty>] as *mut [$ty]) };
[14084](https://docs.rs#14084)                self.copy_to(dst);
[14085](https://docs.rs#14085)                dst
[14086](https://docs.rs#14086)            }
[14087](https://docs.rs#14087)
[14088](https://docs.rs#14088)            /// Copy the contents of the source Rust slice into this
[14089](https://docs.rs#14089)            /// JS typed array.
[14090](https://docs.rs#14090)            ///
[14091](https://docs.rs#14091)            /// This function will efficiently copy the memory from within
[14092](https://docs.rs#14092)            /// the Wasm module's own linear memory to this typed array.
[14093](https://docs.rs#14093)            ///
[14094](https://docs.rs#14094)            /// # Panics
[14095](https://docs.rs#14095)            ///
[14096](https://docs.rs#14096)            /// This function will panic if this typed array's length is
[14097](https://docs.rs#14097)            /// different than the length of the provided `src` array.
[14098](https://docs.rs#14098)            pub fn copy_from(&self, src: &[$ty]) {
[14099](https://docs.rs#14099)                core::assert_eq!(self.length() as usize, src.len());
[14100](https://docs.rs#14100)                self.copy_from_slice(src);
[14101](https://docs.rs#14101)            }
[14102](https://docs.rs#14102)
[14103](https://docs.rs#14103)            /// Efficiently copies the contents of this JS typed array into a new Vec.
[14104](https://docs.rs#14104)            pub fn to_vec(&self) -> Vec<$ty> {
[14105](https://docs.rs#14105)                let len = self.length() as usize;
[14106](https://docs.rs#14106)                let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(len);
[14107](https://docs.rs#14107)                // Safety: the capacity has been set
[14108](https://docs.rs#14108)                unsafe {
[14109](https://docs.rs#14109)                    self.raw_copy_to_ptr(output.as_mut_ptr());
[14110](https://docs.rs#14110)                    output.set_len(len);
[14111](https://docs.rs#14111)                }
[14112](https://docs.rs#14112)                output
[14113](https://docs.rs#14113)            }
[14114](https://docs.rs#14114)        }

[14137](https://docs.rs#14137)    /// `Int8Array()`

# js_sys::Atomics - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/js_sys/Atomics/index.html

## Expand description

The `Atomics` object provides atomic operations as static methods.
They are used with `SharedArrayBuffer` objects.

The Atomic operations are installed on an `Atomics` module. Unlike
the other global objects, `Atomics` is not a constructor. You cannot
use it with a new operator or invoke the `Atomics` object as a
function. All properties and methods of `Atomics` are static
(as is the case with the Math object, for example).
[MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Atomics)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [add](https://docs.rs/fn.add.html)
- The static `Atomics.add()`method adds a given value at a given position in the array and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [add_](https://docs.rs/fn.add_bigint.html)- bigint
- The static `Atomics.add()`method adds a given value at a given position in the array and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [and](https://docs.rs/fn.and.html)
- The static `Atomics.and()`method computes a bitwise AND with a given value at a given position in the array, and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [and_](https://docs.rs/fn.and_bigint.html)- bigint
- The static `Atomics.and()`method computes a bitwise AND with a given value at a given position in the array, and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_exchange.html)- exchange
- The static `Atomics.compareExchange()`method exchanges a given replacement value at a given position in the array, if a given expected value equals the old value. It returns the old value at that position whether it was equal to the expected value or not. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_exchange_bigint.html)- exchange_ - bigint
- The static `Atomics.compareExchange()`method exchanges a given replacement value at a given position in the array, if a given expected value equals the old value. It returns the old value at that position whether it was equal to the expected value or not. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [exchange](https://docs.rs/fn.exchange.html)
- The static `Atomics.exchange()`method stores a given value at a given position in the array and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [exchange_](https://docs.rs/fn.exchange_bigint.html)- bigint
- The static `Atomics.exchange()`method stores a given value at a given position in the array and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_lock_free.html)- lock_ - free

- [notify_](https://docs.rs/fn.notify_with_count.html)- with_ - count

- [or](https://docs.rs/fn.or.html)

- [or_](https://docs.rs/fn.or_bigint.html)- bigint
- The static `Atomics.or()`method computes a bitwise OR with a given value at a given position in the array, and returns the old value at that position. This atomic operation guarantees that no other write happens until the modified value is written back.
- [pause](https://docs.rs/fn.pause.html)
- The static `Atomics.pause()`static method provides a micro-wait primitive that hints to the CPU that the caller is spinning while waiting on access to a shared resource. This allows the system to reduce the resources allocated to the core (such as power) or thread, without yielding the current thread.

# js_sys::JSON - Rust

## Expand description

The `JSON` object contains methods for parsing [JavaScript Object
Notation (JSON)](https://json.org/) and converting values to JSON. It
can’t be called or constructed, and aside from its two method
properties, it has no interesting functionality of its own.

# js_sys::WebAssembly - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/js_sys/WebAssembly/index.html

The WebAssembly.CompileError() constructor creates a new
WebAssembly CompileError object, which indicates an error during
WebAssembly decoding or validation.

A WebAssembly.Instance object is a stateful, executable instance
of a WebAssembly.Module. Instance objects contain all the exported
WebAssembly functions that allow calling into WebAssembly code from
JavaScript.

The WebAssembly.LinkError() constructor creates a new WebAssembly
LinkError object, which indicates an error during module
instantiation (besides traps from the start function).

A WebAssembly.Module object contains stateless WebAssembly code
that has already been compiled by the browser and can be
efficiently shared with Workers, and instantiated multiple times.

The WebAssembly.RuntimeError() constructor creates a new WebAssembly
RuntimeError object — the type that is thrown whenever WebAssembly
specifies a trap.

The WebAssembly.compile() function compiles a WebAssembly.Module
from WebAssembly binary code. This function is useful if it is
necessary to a compile a module before it can be instantiated
(otherwise, the WebAssembly.instantiate() function should be used).

The WebAssembly.compileStreaming() function compiles a
WebAssembly.Module module directly from a streamed underlying
source. This function is useful if it is necessary to a compile a
module before it can be instantiated (otherwise, the
WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming() function should be used).

The WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming() function compiles and
instantiates a WebAssembly module directly from a streamed
underlying source. This is the most efficient, optimized way to load
Wasm code.

The WebAssembly.validate() function validates a given typed
array of WebAssembly binary code, returning whether the bytes
form a valid Wasm module (true) or not (false).

# js_sys::futures - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/js_sys/futures/index.html

## Expand description

Bridging between JavaScript `Promise`s and Rust `Future`s.

Enables `promise.await` directly on any [ Promise](https://docs.rs/struct.Promise.html).
This module is also re-exported by

`wasm-bindgen-futures` for backwards compatibility.
Converting between JavaScript `Promise`s to Rust `Future`s.This module provides a bridge for working with JavaScript `Promise` types as
a Rust `Future`, and similarly contains utilities to turn a rust `Future`
into a JavaScript `Promise`. This can be useful when working with
asynchronous or otherwise blocking work in Rust (wasm), and provides the
ability to interoperate with JavaScript events and JavaScript I/O
primitives.

There are three main interfaces in this module currently:

-
A type that is constructed with a `Promise`and can then be used as a`Future<Output = Result<JsValue, JsValue>>`. This Rust future will resolve or reject with the value coming out of the`Promise`.
-
Converts a Rust `Future<Output = Result<JsValue, JsValue>>`into a JavaScript`Promise`. The future’s result will translate to either a resolved or rejected`Promise`in JavaScript.
-
Spawns a `Future<Output = ()>`on the current thread. This is the best way to run a`Future`in Rust without sending it to JavaScript.

These three items should provide enough of a bridge to interoperate the two systems and make sure that Rust/JavaScript can work together with asynchronous and I/O work.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [JsFuture](https://docs.rs/struct.JsFuture.html)
- A Rust `Future`backed by a JavaScript`Promise`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [future_](https://docs.rs/fn.future_to_promise.html)- to_ - promise
- Converts a Rust `Future`into a JavaScript`Promise`.
- [future_](https://docs.rs/fn.future_to_promise_typed.html)- to_ - promise_ - typed
- Converts a Rust `Future`into a corresponding typed JavaScript`Promise<T>`.
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_local.html)- local
- Runs a Rust `Future`on the current thread.

# AggregateError in js_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/js_sys/struct.AggregateError.html

`pub struct AggregateError { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `AggregateError` object represents an error when several errors need
to be wrapped in a single error. It is thrown when multiple errors need
to be reported by an operation, for example by [ Promise::any](https://docs.rs/struct.Promise.html#method.any), when
all promises passed to it reject.

`AggregateError` is a subclass of [ Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html).

Returns the `f64` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
number.

If this JS value is not an instance of a number then this returns
`None`.

If this JS value is a string value, this function copies the JS string
value into Wasm linear memory, encoded as UTF-8, and returns it as a
Rust `String`.

To avoid the copying and re-encoding, consider the
`JsString::try_from()` function from [js-sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys)
instead.

If this JS value is not an instance of a string or if it’s not valid
utf-8 then this returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#utf-16-vs-utf-8)UTF-16 vs UTF-8

JavaScript strings in general are encoded as UTF-16, but Rust strings
are encoded as UTF-8. This can cause the Rust string to look a bit
different than the JS string sometimes. For more details see the
[documentation about the  str type](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html) which contains a few
caveats about the encodings.

Returns the `bool` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
boolean.

If this JS value is not an instance of a boolean then this returns
`None`.

The `Array.fromAsync()` static method with a map function creates a new, shallow-copied
`Array` instance from an async iterable, iterable or array-like object, applying the map
function to each value.

The `findIndex()` method returns the index of the first element in the array that
satisfies the provided testing function. Otherwise -1 is returned.

**Note:** Consider using [ Array::try_find_index](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html#method.try_find_index) if the predicate might throw an error.

The `findLast()` method of Array instances iterates the array in reverse order
and returns the value of the first element that satisfies the provided testing function.
If no elements satisfy the testing function, undefined is returned.

#### pub fn [set_length](https://docs.rs#method.set_length)(&self, value: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html))

Sets the length of the array.

If it is set to less than the current length of the array, it will shrink the array.

If it is set to more than the current length of the array, it will increase the length of the array, filling the new space with empty slots.

`map()` calls a provided callback function once for each element in an array,
in order, and constructs a new array from the results. callback is invoked
only for indexes of the array which have assigned values, including undefined.
It is not called for missing elements of the array (that is, indexes that have
never been set, which have been deleted or which have never been assigned a value).

**Note:** Consider using [ Array::try_map](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html#method.try_map) for safer fallible handling.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#526)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#526)

`map()` calls a provided callback function once for each element in an array,
in order, and constructs a new array from the results. callback is invoked
only for indexes of the array which have assigned values, including undefined.
It is not called for missing elements of the array (that is, indexes that have
never been set, which have been deleted or which have never been assigned a value).
*(Fallible variation)*

The `Array.of()` method creates a new Array instance with a variable
number of arguments, regardless of number or type of the arguments.

Note: For type inference use `Array::<T>::of(&[T])`.

The difference between `Array.of()` and the `Array` constructor is in the
handling of integer arguments: `Array.of(7)` creates an array with a single
element, `7`, whereas `Array(7)` creates an empty array with a `length`
property of `7` (Note: this implies an array of 7 empty slots, not slots
with actual undefined values).

The `shift()` method removes the first element from an array and returns
that removed element. This method changes the length of the array.

**Note:** Consider using [ Array::shift_checked](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html#method.shift_checked) for handling empty arrays.

The `some()` method tests whether at least one element in the array passes the test implemented
by the provided function.
Note: This method returns false for any condition put on an empty array.

**Note:** Consider using [ Array::try_some](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html#method.try_some) if the predicate might throw an error.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#526)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#526)

The `some()` method tests whether at least one element in the array passes the test implemented

Note: This method returns false for any condition put on an empty array.
[MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/some)

The `sort()` method sorts the elements of an array in place and returns
the array. The sort is not necessarily stable. The default sort
order is according to string Unicode code points.

The time and space complexity of the sort cannot be guaranteed as it is implementation dependent.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#2097-2105)#### pub fn [from_iter_typed](https://docs.rs#method.from_iter_typed)<A, I>(iter: I) -> [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html)<T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/js_sys/lib.rs.html#2097-2105)

#### pub fn [from_iter_typed](https://docs.rs#method.from_iter_typed)<A, I>(iter: I) -> [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html)<T>

Collect an iterator into a typed `Array<T>`, projecting each item
through its canonical [ JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/trait.JsGeneric.html) via

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html)

`IntoJsGeneric`This is the typed counterpart to the stable
`impl FromIterator<A> for Array where A: AsRef<JsValue>`, which always
produces an erased `Array<JsValue>`. Use `from_iter_typed` when you
want the element type inferred from the iterator item:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use js_sys::{Array, Number};
let arr = Array::from_iter_typed((0..10).map(Number::from));
// arr: Array<Number>
```
Reference iteration (`Item = &U`) is supported transparently via the
`&U: IntoJsGeneric` blanket in `wasm-bindgen` core.

Use `Object::hasOwn` instead.

[Source](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/wasm_bindgen/lib.rs.html#191)

[Source](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/wasm_bindgen/lib.rs.html#194)

[Source](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/wasm_bindgen/lib.rs.html#197)

Returns the `f64` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
number.

If this JS value is not an instance of a number then this returns
`None`.

If this JS value is a string value, this function copies the JS string
value into Wasm linear memory, encoded as UTF-8, and returns it as a
Rust `String`.

To avoid the copying and re-encoding, consider the
`JsString::try_from()` function from [js-sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys)
instead.

If this JS value is not an instance of a string or if it’s not valid
utf-8 then this returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#utf-16-vs-utf-8)UTF-16 vs UTF-8

JavaScript strings in general are encoded as UTF-16, but Rust strings
are encoded as UTF-8. This can cause the Rust string to look a bit
different than the JS string sometimes. For more details see the
[documentation about the  str type](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html) which contains a few
caveats about the encodings.

Returns the `bool` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
boolean.

If this JS value is not an instance of a boolean then this returns
`None`.

Returns the `f64` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
number.

If this JS value is not an instance of a number then this returns
`None`.

If this JS value is a string value, this function copies the JS string
value into Wasm linear memory, encoded as UTF-8, and returns it as a
Rust `String`.

To avoid the copying and re-encoding, consider the
`JsString::try_from()` function from [js-sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys)
instead.

If this JS value is not an instance of a string or if it’s not valid
utf-8 then this returns `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#utf-16-vs-utf-8)UTF-16 vs UTF-8

JavaScript strings in general are encoded as UTF-16, but Rust strings
are encoded as UTF-8. This can cause the Rust string to look a bit
different than the JS string sometimes. For more details see the
[documentation about the  str type](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html) which contains a few
caveats about the encodings.

Returns the `bool` value of this JS value if it’s an instance of a
boolean.

If this JS value is not an instance of a boolean then this returns
`None`.

Creates a JS typed array which is a view into wasm’s linear memory at the slice specified.

This function returns a new typed array which is a view into wasm’s memory. This view does not copy the underlying data.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

Views into WebAssembly memory are only valid so long as the
backing buffer isn’t resized in JS. Once this function is called
any future calls to `Box::new` (or malloc of any form) may cause
the returned value here to be invalidated. Use with caution!

Additionally the returned object can be safely mutated but the input slice isn’t guaranteed to be mutable.

Finally, the returned object is disconnected from the input slice’s lifetime, so there’s no guarantee that the data is read at the right time.
